newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Fitzcarraldo returns opera to the Amazon. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New Fitzcarraldo returns opera to the Amazon. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]

text.p: After 90 years of silence, strains of the music of Verdi, Rossini and Bizet will once again fill the small Amazon Theatre this weekend when the city of Manaus hosts its first international opera festival.

Over a period of two weeks, music-lovers in this remote Amazon city will have a chance to listen to such classics as "La Traviata," "Carmen" and "The Barber of Seville" performed by a troupe of world-class voices.

Singers have been recruited from the Colon Theatre in Buenos Aires, Latin America's foremost opera venue, while the music will be played by the Minsk Opera Orchestra (corrects from Moscow's Bolshoi Opera Orchestra), conducted by Urs Schneider.

It will be Manaus's first opera season since 1907, the year the 680-seat Belle Epoque theatre was forced to close when the bottom fell out of Brazil's 20-year rubber boom and most of the city's opera buffs declared themselves broke.
The revived festival was the brainchild of Michael Jelden, a 25-year-old German concert violinist who discovered the existence of the Amazon Theatre while browsing on the Internet.
"From that moment on, I couldn't stop thinking about the idea of an empty opera house sitting in the middle of the rainforest," Jelden told Reuters in an interview.
He said that even before his first trip to Manaus in September last year, he had already decided to stage the music festival.
Jelden recalls he stood before the city of Manaus authorities and said to them: "If you want opera, then give me the opera house."
He said they hesitated for a moment, and then gave him the go-ahead. Six months later, Jelden is staging what he pompously describes as "Latin America's biggest music festival."

Newspapers have dubbed Jelden "the new Fitzcarraldo" after the central character in Werner Herzog's classic movie "Fitzcarraldo" that tells the story of a man obsessed with taking opera to the Amazon Indians.
But the young musician objected to the comparison, saying he had never heard of Herzog's movie before becoming involved with the music festival.
The Manaus International Opera festival will run from April 5 to April 20.
